issues.description: README bundles unrelated rewrites including a StorageError.handle signature reorder
issues.detail: The README diff reorders handle(ex, req, resp, params) to (req, resp, ex, params) and reformats large portions unrelated to the PR's stated purpose of adding POST tests. This scope creep increases regression risk, complicates review, and may mislead users on older Falcon versions. Split cosmetic/API-doc changes into a separate PR.

issues.description: FAQ example teaches req.stream.read(content_length) — the very anti-pattern the PR fixes elsewhere
issues.detail: The FAQ PostTest uses req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0), which is exactly the unsafe pattern things_advanced.py switches away from (to bounded_stream). The behavior with Content-Length=1 and an empty body is WSGI-server dependent, so asserting HTTP 400 is fragile and contradicts guidance shipped in the same PR.

issues.description: PR description mismatches diff and switch to bounded_stream lacks rationale/newsfragment
issues.detail: Description claims req.content_length was added to req.stream.read(), but the diff actually switches to req.bounded_stream.read() with no length argument. This is a meaningful behavioral change (bounded vs raw, different handling of missing/chunked Content-Length) without an explanatory comment or towncrier fragment despite the checklist claiming one.

issues.description: New tests assert only status_code and may not exercise the bug being fixed
issues.detail: resp4 expects 400 for empty body with Content-Length:1, but bounded_stream returns b'' regardless and the test doesn't distinguish auth/JSON/empty 400 paths. Asserting on title/description or Location header for resp3 would catch regressions; as written the tests may pass for incidental reasons and don't clearly validate the bounded_stream fix.

issues.description: FAQ code snippet has unidiomatic style (parenthesized assert, trailing comma, missing blank lines)
issues.detail: The snippet uses assert(result.status == ...) which looks like a function call (common pytest anti-pattern), has a stray trailing comma in headers = [('Content-Length', '1'),], and misses PEP 8 blank lines between definitions. Since the FAQ is user-facing teaching material, it should model idiomatic Python.

issues.description: Tests don't cover ASGI path despite checklist claim of WSGI+ASGI coverage
issues.detail: test_things_advanced accepts asgi/httpx/requests fixtures but the new POST assertions only exercise advanced.app via testing.simulate_post (WSGI). The PR checklist claims both code paths were updated; either parametrize across ASGI or correct the checklist.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a clear verdict: the underlying change (switching things_advanced.py to req.bounded_stream.read() plus two POST tests) is small and reasonable, but the PR bundles a sprawling unrelated README rewrite — including a StorageError.handle signature reorder — that should be split out. The FAQ example teaches req.stream.read(content_length), directly contradicting the bounded_stream fix shipped in the same PR, and relies on WSGI-server-dependent behavior. The new tests assert only on status_code and don't clearly demonstrate the bug being fixed. The PR description mismatches the actual diff, and minor style/coverage issues round out the concerns.
